text: For dx/dt = Ax where A has a size-k Jordan block for a purely imaginary eigenvalue (Re lambda = 0), solutions:
choices: force the eigenvalue to be real
explanation: A nontrivial Jordan block contributes terms t^{k-1} e^{lambda t}; with Re lambda = 0 the magnitude grows like t^{k-1}, so the marginal equilibrium is actually unstable. Only simple (diagonalizable) eigenvalues on the axis give bounded solutions.
